sentences.En ulv og en hund kom i snakk med hveran: A wolf and a dog got talking to each other.
sentences.Ulven var så sulten og tynn. Den kunne n: The wolf was so hungry and thin. It could hardly stand on its legs.
sentences.Det er vanskelige tider, sa ulven til hu: These are hard times, said the wolf to the dog. I can hardly get hold of anything to eat.
Then we can share my job, said the dog.
sentences.Jeg bor hos menneskene, og de kommer med: I live with the humans, and they bring me meat and give me everything I need every day.
sentences.Det var en fantastisk idé, sa ulven, jeg: That's a fantastic idea, said the wolf, I'll come and live with you right away.
sentences.Så fikk den øye på noe rundt hundens hal: Then it noticed something around the dog's neck.
sentences.Hva er det du har rundt halsen? spurte d: What's that you have around your neck? it asked.
sentences.Å det ... Det er bare halsbåndet mitt, d: Oh, that ... That's just my collar, said the dog.
sentences.Menneskene bruker det for å binde meg fa: The humans use it to tie me up outside the house.
sentences.Mener du at du ikke kan komme og gå som: Do you mean you can't come and go as you like? asked the wolf.
sentences.Jeg må jo holde meg i nærheten av huset: Well, I have to stay near the house when I'm looking after the humans and keeping watch over the house, explained the dog.
sentences.Da løp ulven tilbake til skogen igjen, o: Then the wolf ran back to the forest, and it never thought about sharing a job with the dog again.
